title: APPROVING THE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY OF CERTAIN DOCUMENTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE ISSUANCE BY THE ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY OF ONE OR MORE SERIES OF ITS ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION
text:
RESOLUTION NO. ____________ - APPROVING THE EXECUTION AND DELIVERY OF CERTAIN DOCUMENTS IN CONNECTION WITH THE ISSUANCE BY THE ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY OF ONE OR MORE SERIES OF ITS ALAMEDA CORRIDOR TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY SUBORDINATE LIEN REVENUE REFUNDING BONDS AND SECOND SUBORDINATE LIEN REVENUE REFUNDING BONDS AND AUTHORIZING SUCH OTHER ACTIONS AS ARE NECESSARY TO ASSIST THE AUTHORITY IN THE ISSUANCE OF SUCH REFUNDING BONDS AND MAKING A DETERMINATION RELATING HERETO
Summary
: Staff requests approval of certain documents related to the proposed issuance of the Alameda Corridor Transportation Authority (ACTA) Subordinate Lien Revenue Refunding Bonds and Second Subordinate Lien Revenue Refunding Bonds (2026 ACTA Bonds) including certain disclosures required from the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department (Harbor Department). The proposed action is aligned with the Harbor Department’s Strategic Plan, Objective 3: Improved Performance of Port Assets. Given the Harbor Department’s role as a partial guarantor of ACTA’s debt along with the Port of Long Beach, it must provide certain financial and operating disclosures to the bond market for any ACTA bond transactions, both at the time of the initial offering and for as long as the bonds remain outstanding. ACTA is projecting that its existing cash reserves and future revenues will be insufficient to cover debt service payments over a 13-year period from Fiscal Year (FY) 2028 through FY 2040, and that Shortfall Advances would be required from the two ports to offset the difference. Currently, ACTA projects that the Harbor Department would be responsible for approximately $22.4 million in average annual Shortfall Advances over this 13-year period. Under the proposed transaction, the two ports’ annual average Shortfall Advances would be reduced by extending the duration over which Shortfall Advances are made. Under the proposed transaction, ACTA projects that the Harbor Department would be responsible for approximately $17.7 million in average annual Shortfall Advances over a 17-year period from FY 2028 through FY 2044. Bond market conditions at the time of the transaction and ACTA’s future revenues will determine the level of Shortfall Advance savings that will ultimately be achieved.
Recommendation
: Board resolve to 1) find that the Director of Environmental Management has determined that the proposed action is administratively exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under Article II, Section 2(f) of the Los Angeles City CEQA Guidelines; 2) authorize the execution and delivery of the Continuing Disclosure Certificate, the Letter of Representation, and other related documents and certificates in connection with the issuance and sale of the 2026 ACTA Bonds; 3) authorize the City of Los Angeles Harbor Department’s Executive Director or Chief Financial Officer, each of them acting individually, to comply with the terms and intent of the Board’s Resolution, to assist ACTA in the issuance of the 2026 ACTA Bonds, to execute and deliver any documents or instruments related thereto and to take such other actions as may be deemed necessary or desirable in order to carry out the purposes of the Board’s Resolution subject to: (i) approval of the issuance of the 2026 ACTA Bonds by ACTA, and (ii) the conditions set forth in the Resolution; 4) approve certain disclosures relating to the finances and operations of the Harbor Department to be contained in the Preliminary Official Statement and the Official Statement for the 2026 ACTA Bonds including the Audited Financial Statements of the Harbor Department, with such changes thereto as the Executive Director or the Chief Financial Officer may require or approve; and 5) adopt Resolution No. __________.
